acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Boars family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Bristle Hog, T1, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Straight-Line Initiate archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two fire construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Compact wild hog with raised bristles, short tusks, low ordinary body, and clean unscarred flanks.
Signature mechanic: Two-Scrape Charge: one forehoof paws twice before the Hog launches along its fixed head line.
battlefieldDuty: Make one short straight charge that cannot turn after a single scrape.
constructionDimensions: Bristle tips char and flare backward from acceleration while ember seams remain localized to tusk roots and shoulder calluses.
Hoof sparks, smoke trails, and brief burning furrows reveal charge direction and cool after impact.
counterplay: Sidestep the fixed lane and punish the exposed flank during its stop. Affinity signal: The loaded shoulder and tusk root brighten before the charge, then expose a cooling seam on collision.
identityInvariants: Every form keeps a low four-legged boar body, cloven hooves, mobile snout, raised bristles, short tail, and visible tusk roots.
Tier escalation uses tusk geometry, neck mass, shoulder callus, scars, and bristle profile rather than humanoid equipment.
Charge direction remains readable through hoof placement, lowered head angle, tusk contact, dust, and the alignment of the spine.
telegraph: The forehoof scrapes twice and the head lowers between the shoulders.
